entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "We were in the middle of a meeting..."
entries.dialogueText: We were in the middle of a meeting in the Palace about our immigration policy.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "The ensuing discussion quickly beca..."
entries.dialogueText: The ensuing discussion quickly became heated.

entries.speaker: Iosef Lancea
entries.title: Iosef Lancea: "“It just doesn't make any sense to..."
entries.dialogueText: “It just doesn't make any sense to me that a foreign citizen should come before a Sordish citizen. In Sordland!”

entries.speaker: Iosef Lancea
entries.title: Iosef Lancea: "“I don't think so, Mr. Wisci!”"
entries.dialogueText: “I don't think so, Mr. Wisci!”

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: "“Immigrants are the reason our econ..."
entries.dialogueText: “Immigrants are the reason our economy is not completely unsalvageable.”

entries.speaker: Lileas Graf
entries.title: Lileas Graf: "“Well said. My analysis is also in..."
entries.dialogueText: “Well said. My analysis is also in line with this. Especially during the economic recession... We are giving Sordish jobs to migrants from other countries. What about our own people?”

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: "“Statistically speaking, allowing i..."
entries.dialogueText: “Statistically speaking, allowing immigrants to become part of the workforce contributes to our economy. But I agree that the current situation is very nuanced.”

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: "“With that said, we can't just tigh..."
entries.dialogueText: “With that said, we can't just tighten our immigration policy and expect the economy to stay the same.”

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: "“Look at Agnolian immigrants in Agn..."
entries.dialogueText: “Look at Agnolian immigrants in Agnland. They have revitalized the whole region and in turn, boosted the economy of the entire country. Symon can attest to that.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“We need to consider the impact on..."
entries.dialogueText: “We need to consider the impact on economy.”
entries.menuText: “I agree that we need to consider the economic impact of immigration.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“We need to modernize and reach the..."
entries.dialogueText: “We need to modernize and reach the level of the superpowers.”
entries.menuText: “We need to modernize and reach the level of the superpowers.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Sordish citizens must come first.”"
entries.dialogueText: “Sordish citizens must come first.”
entries.menuText: “Sordish citizens must come first.”

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: "“Our money flow should be our utmos..."
entries.dialogueText: “Our money flow should be our utmost concern, if we want to have the capability to accomplish actual change.”

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: "“Look at the superpowers. Do you se..."
entries.dialogueText: “Look at the superpowers. Do you see them closing off their borders? Why do you think their economies are in such good shape? They are in their current state because they welcome immigration, and use it to their advantage.”

entries.speaker: Iosef Lancea
entries.title: Iosef Lancea: "“Exactly. Our citizens should never..."
entries.dialogueText: “Exactly. Our citizens should never feel threatened by foreigners.”

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: "“I am of the same mind. It is prove..."
entries.dialogueText: “I am of the same mind. It is proven that immigration helps countries to develop. And we cannot just deport our current immigrants.”

entries.dialogueText: “We need a decision. But before we move on...”

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: "“Mr. President. Do you have any que..."
entries.dialogueText: “Mr. President. Do you have any questions about the current state of immigration?”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“What is the current legal status o..."
entries.dialogueText: “What is the current legal status of immigrants?”
entries.menuText: “What is the current legal status of immigrants?”

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: "“Currently, all accepted immigrants..."
entries.dialogueText: “Currently, all accepted immigrants are given a work permit on arrival, so that they can work and contribute to the economy of Sordland. There is currently no limit on the number of immigrants accepted. However, the number has remained stable over the past years.”

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: "“Despite the laws, the fact is many..."
entries.dialogueText: “Despite the laws, the fact is many immigrants illegally work for corporations. That is the main issue with immigration right now. Not the immigration itself.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“How many immigrants live in Sordla..."
entries.dialogueText: “How many immigrants live in Sordland?”
entries.menuText: “How many immigrants live in Sordland?”

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: "“Official numbers show that we have..."
entries.dialogueText: “Official numbers show that we have anywhere between two to three million immigrants residing in Sordland.”

entries.speaker: Lileas Graf
entries.title: Lileas Graf: "“Even excluding the countless undoc..."
entries.dialogueText: “Even excluding the countless undocumented aliens in our midst, that is a very substantial amount. The primary issue is the strife they cause between less fortunate Sordish citizens and themselves.”

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: "“Including them in the workforce wo..."
entries.dialogueText: “Including them in the workforce would benefit everybody, including unemployed Sords. More taxes means more services.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“How do immigrants usually arrive h..."
entries.dialogueText: “How do immigrants usually arrive here?”
entries.menuText: “How do immigrants usually arrive here?”

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: "“There are three major paths they c..."
entries.dialogueText: “There are three major paths they choose. The first one is the Agnland to Agnolia border. The second is the Bergia to Wehlen border, and the third is the Lorren Coast.”

entries.speaker: Iosef Lancea
entries.title: Iosef Lancea: "“Agnolians are the largest group. I..."
entries.dialogueText: “Agnolians are the largest group. It's a light border over there. Although recently, political fugitives from Valgsland have been crossing the Grey Sea by boat to land on our coast.”

entries.speaker: Lileas Graf
entries.title: Lileas Graf: "“Politically persecuted Wehzek refu..."
entries.dialogueText: “Politically persecuted Wehzek refugees tend to use the dangerous mountain passes at the Wehlen border. Many of them also have Bludish blood. This is significantly increasing the Blud populace inside Bergia.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Let's move on and see what can be..."
entries.dialogueText: “Let's move on and see what can be done about the immigration situation.”
entries.menuText: “Let's move on and see what can be done about the immigration situation.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“I don't have any questions. Let's..."
entries.dialogueText: “I don't have any questions. Let's move on to solutions.”
entries.menuText: “I don't have any questions. Let's move on to solutions.”

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: "“Very well.”"
entries.dialogueText: “Very well.”

entries.speaker: Lileas Graf
entries.title: Lileas Graf: "“Nonsense. If not for the unlimited..."
entries.dialogueText: “Nonsense. If not for the unlimited amount of immigration, we wouldn't be in this state.”

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Deivid Wisci opened his dossier sta..."
entries.dialogueText: Deivid Wisci opened his dossier stamped with the seal of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade.

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: "“Before we make any decisions, I ha..."
entries.dialogueText: “Before we make any decisions, I have to remind you.”

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: "“During the elections, we promised..."
entries.dialogueText: “During the elections, we promised to tighten immigration laws. Of course, as you know, I was and I still am against it.”

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: "“During the elections we promised t..."
entries.dialogueText: “During the elections we promised to keep our immigration laws relaxed. Which I think is the right course of action.”

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: "“I agree with Deivid. We can turn i..."
entries.dialogueText: “I agree with Deivid. We can turn immigration to our advantage from a financial standpoint.”

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: "“I see your point, Iosef but the ec..."
entries.dialogueText: “I see your point, Iosef but the economy certainly benefits from more immigration.”

entries.speaker: Iosef Lancea
entries.title: Iosef Lancea: "“I disagree. We are supposed to con..."
entries.dialogueText: “I disagree. We are supposed to control and reduce the negative effects of immigration, like crime and subversion.”

entries.speaker: Lileas Graf
entries.title: Lileas Graf: "“Internal order on the other hand,..."
entries.dialogueText: “Internal order on the other hand, suffers immensely.”

entries.speaker: Iosef Lancea
entries.title: Iosef Lancea: "“We need to keep our promises and f..."
entries.dialogueText: “We need to keep our promises and focus on our own citizens. That is what I think.”

entries.speaker: Lileas Graf
entries.title: Lileas Graf: "“We should tighten the laws to prev..."
entries.dialogueText: “We should tighten the laws to prevent further chaos.”

entries.speaker: Lileas Graf
entries.title: Lileas Graf: "“Believe me, it would surprise you...."
entries.dialogueText: “Believe me, it would surprise you.”

entries.speaker: Lileas Graf
entries.title: Lileas Graf: "“Advantage? You should go over the..."
entries.dialogueText: “Advantage? You should go over the amount of disadvantages caused by immigrants. I can provide you with a report from my ministry later.”

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: "“This is going nowhere.”"
entries.dialogueText: “This is going nowhere.”

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Deivid sighed wearily."
entries.dialogueText: Deivid sighed wearily.

entries.dialogueText: “What are the consequences of keeping our immigration policy relaxed?”
entries.menuText: “What are the consequences of keeping our immigration policy relaxed?”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“I am ready to make a decision.”"
entries.dialogueText: “I am ready to make a decision.”
entries.menuText: “I am ready to make a decision.”

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: "“We would have to impose quotas and..."
entries.dialogueText: “We would have to impose quotas and, connected to that, stricter border control.”

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: "“On top of allowing our economy to..."
entries.dialogueText: “On top of allowing our economy to take a hit.”

entries.speaker: Lileas Graf
entries.title: Lileas Graf: "“Mr. Holl. Surely the well-being of..."
entries.dialogueText: “Mr. Holl. Surely the well-being of our citizens and our internal security will more than compensate for any downturn in the markets."

entries.speaker: Iosef Lancea
entries.title: Iosef Lancea: "“Agreed. Sordish citizens should ta..."
entries.dialogueText: “Agreed. Sordish citizens should take priority.”

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: "“Aside from keeping us on the path..."
entries.dialogueText: “Aside from keeping us on the path to prosperity, modernity and continuous improvement...Not much. Our current system is good for our era. We also have the capacity.”

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: "“This will allow us to continue pro..."
entries.dialogueText: “This will allow us to continue protecting investments from foreign countries, which in turn will keep our trade steady. We would be more trustworthy partners. Stability draws money.”

entries.speaker: Lileas Graf
entries.title: Lileas Graf: "“Stability? What stability? We're a..."
entries.dialogueText: “Stability? What stability? We're already seeing clashes between our people and foreign interlopers. On the contrary, the only way we can achieve stability is through tightening our immigration policy.”

entries.speaker: Iosef Lancea
entries.title: Iosef Lancea: "“You heard the lady. Sordland first..."
entries.dialogueText: “You heard the lady. Sordland first...”

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: "“Yes?”"
entries.dialogueText: “Yes?”

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Everyone leaned forward, eager to h..."
entries.dialogueText: Everyone leaned forward, eager to hear my response.

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“We will keep immigration laws rela..."
entries.dialogueText: “We will keep immigration laws relaxed.”
entries.menuText: “We will keep immigration laws relaxed.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“We'll tighten our immigration laws..."
entries.dialogueText: “We'll tighten our immigration laws. I'll sign the decree soon, so be prepared to start working on it, Mr. Wisci.”
entries.menuText: “We'll tighten our immigration laws. I'll sign the decree soon, so be prepared to start working on it, Mr. Wisci.”

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: "“I am glad you made the right choic..."
entries.dialogueText: “I am glad you made the right choice.”

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci

entries.dialogueText: “It is unfortunate to see Sordland move in this direction... But I trust you have good intentions. I'll move ahead with the implementation."

entries.title: Iosef Lancea: "“We will be forced to handle new wa..."
entries.dialogueText: “We will be forced to handle new waves of migrants from Agnolia. Our border posts aren't ready.”

entries.dialogueText: “This has the chance to affect our trade negotiations with Agnolia negatively. They expect us to respect the flow of people.”

entries.speaker: Lileas Graf
entries.title: Lileas Graf: "“Also, this will bring a new tide o..."
entries.dialogueText: “Also, this will bring a new tide of refugees from Wehlen. Bergia is already a difficult region to manage.”

entries.speaker: Iosef Lancea
entries.title: Iosef Lancea: "“Anything else that needs to be sai..."
entries.dialogueText: “Anything else that needs to be said?”

entries.speaker: Lileas Graf
entries.title: Lileas Graf: "“Not only that, we've just abandone..."
entries.dialogueText: “Not only that, we've just abandoned the native Sords who need our support the most.”

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: "“This will isolate us in every way...."
entries.dialogueText: “This will isolate us in every way. The more we are connected to the world, the better.”

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "The ministers gathered their docume..."
entries.dialogueText: The ministers gathered their documents and rose from their chairs, some with frowns on their faces.

entries.speaker: Iosef Lancea
entries.title: Iosef Lancea: "“This is shameful.”"
entries.dialogueText: “This is shameful.”

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: "“Indeed. It will be a challenge to..."
entries.dialogueText: “Indeed. It will be a challenge to convince these countries as they see our borders close.”

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: "“Not only that, we've already sligh..."
entries.dialogueText: “Not only that, we've already slighted Wehlen in the past. They might see this as a return to the '30s, which will definitely affect our negotiations.”

entries.speaker: Lileas Graf
entries.title: Lileas Graf: "“If we are finished, I need to head..."
entries.dialogueText: “If we are finished, I need to head off and get the Ministry to work on the new policy.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“The citizens of Sordland aren't fo..."
entries.dialogueText: “The citizens of Sordland aren't forgotten. Our work for them continues.”
entries.menuText: “The citizens of Sordland aren't forgotten. Our work for them continues.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“My decision is final and irreversi..."
entries.dialogueText: “My decision is final and irreversible. Time to move on.”
entries.menuText: “My decision is final and irreversible. Time to move on.”

entries.dialogueText: “We are not leaving Sordland unprotected. It is a logical decision.”
entries.menuText: “We are not leaving Sordland unprotected. It is a logical decision.”

entries.speaker: Symon Holl

entries.dialogueText: “I'm against isolationism. It is the wrong path.”

entries.speaker: Player

entries.dialogueText: “Thank you for your contributions. Let's wrap this up.”
entries.menuText: “Thank you for your contributions. Let's wrap this up.”

entries.dialogueText: “We can't let internal policy be decided by foreigners. Sordland always comes first.”
entries.menuText: “We can't let internal policy be decided by foreigners. Sordland always comes first.”

entries.speaker: Player

entries.dialogueText: “This is not about isolating Sordland, but protecting it.”
entries.menuText: “This is not about isolating Sordland, but protecting it.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“I want everybody here to get used..."
entries.dialogueText: “I want everybody here to get used to the new changes. This is our new direction.”
entries.menuText: “I want everybody here to get used to the new changes. This is our new direction.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Let's end this discussion and get..."
entries.dialogueText: “Let's end this discussion and get to work. There are changes to be made.”
entries.menuText: “Let's end this discussion and get to work. There are changes to be made.”

entries.speaker: Iosef Lancea
entries.title: Iosef Lancea: "“You are wrong about this. There is..."
entries.dialogueText: “You are wrong about this. There is a reason why this country has survived the Century of Revolutions.”

entries.dialogueText: “Both can be a factor in decision-making. We shouldn't forget about the immigrants who live here.”

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci

entries.dialogueText: “Rightfully so.”

entries.speaker: Lileas Graf

entries.dialogueText: “Anything else, Mr. President?”

entries.speaker: Lileas Graf

entries.dialogueText: “Same here. Our border units need to be informed and prepared.”
